title: 8 משחקים וספרים שיעזרו להם לעבוד כצוות

stage.need: Working together at around ages 4 to 5. CDC 4 years: 'Playing with others helps you child learn the value of sharing and friendship' and the tip to teach skills for playing with others such as sharing toys and taking turns; CDC 5 years milestone: 'Follows rules or takes turns when playing games with other children'; KidsHealth: a board game is a peaceful way for children to spend time together. Cooperative games give everyone the same goal, books give characters who solve a problem together.
stage.age_caveat: Ages are approximate: CDC milestones are what most children (75% or more) do by an age, not a deadline. Some 5 year olds wait for a turn easily and some need more time; the frame says בסביבות and the caption says יש ילדים ש.... Weekly batch 2026-10-18, slot 4, first carousel.

dev_sources.title: Milestones by 4 Years
dev_sources.publisher: CDC, Learn the Signs. Act Early. (date reviewed 16 May 2026)
dev_sources.quote: Pretends to be something else during play (teacher, superhero, dog) / Playing with others helps you child learn the value of sharing and friendship. / Continue to teach your child skills to play with others, such as using words, sharing toys, and taking turns. / Join him in pretend play, such as eating the pretend food he cooks. / Read with your child. Ask him what's happening in the story and what he thinks might happen next.
dev_sources.supports: 4 year milestone and tips: pretend play, learning the value of sharing and friendship by playing with others, practising words, sharing toys and taking turns, joining pretend play, and asking about the story while reading. Read today through a page fetch (the CDC site blocks plain curl); sentences quoted as returned and joined with ' / '. The page's own typo ('you child') is kept in the quote.

dev_sources.title: Milestones by 5 Years
dev_sources.publisher: CDC, Learn the Signs. Act Early. (date reviewed 16 May 2026)
dev_sources.quote: Follows rules or takes turns when playing games with other children / Tells a story she heard or made up with at least two events. For example, a cat was stuck in a tree and a firefighter saved it / Teach your child to follow rules in games. For example, play simple board games, card games, or Simon Says. / Encourage your child to pretend play. Help your child find items she can use to play dress up, school, or house. / Keep a box of crayons, paper, paint, child scissors, and glue for creative play.
dev_sources.supports: 5 year milestones and tips: following rules or taking turns in games with other children, telling a story she heard or made up, playing simple board and card games, pretend play and creative play. Read today through a page fetch (the CDC site blocks plain curl); sentences quoted as returned and joined with ' / '. Milestones are what most children do by that age, not a deadline.

dev_sources.title: Sibling Rivalry
dev_sources.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (medically reviewed by Jennifer Shroff Pendley, PhD)
dev_sources.quote: Have fun together as a family. Whether you're watching a movie, throwing a ball, or playing a board game, you're establishing a peaceful way for your kids to spend time together and relate to each other. / Remember, as kids cope with conflict, they also learn important skills that will serve them for life — like how to value another person's point of view, how to compromise and negotiate, and how to control aggressive impulses.
dev_sources.supports: Family fun such as a board game is a peaceful way for children to spend time together, and coping with conflict builds compromise and negotiation. A general parent explainer about siblings, not research on any product here; our copy says practise and opportunity, never a result.
